items.originalTitle: Inside the competition building F1’s future engineering talent
items.summaryEn: Hundreds of students from around the world competed in Singapore at the STEM Racing World Final, a long-running engineering competition that is gaining relevance as a potential pathway into Formula 1 and motorsports. Team Lynx Racing from Saudi Arabia won the four-day international engineering competition and received the 2026 trophy on the actual grand prix podium.
detailZh: 走进这项培养F1未来工程人才的竞赛
来自世界各地的数百名学生在Singapore参加STEM Racing世界总决赛，这项长期举办的工程竞赛正日益成为通往一级方程式和赛车运动的潜在途径
六名沙特阿拉伯高中生，四名男生和两名女生，正兴奋地在Singapore F1围场里来回走动。
他们被称为Lynx Racing队，是年度STEM Racing世界总决赛的新科冠军，该赛事在大奖赛前一周于Singapore举行。在这场为期四天的国际工程竞赛中脱颖而出后，Lynx Racing在真正的大奖赛领奖台上获颁2026年奖杯，其间他们见到了两届世界冠军费尔南多·阿隆索等人，并参观了阿斯顿·马丁车库。
他们中的一些人希望这不是他们最后一次近距离看到F1车库——下一次，他们将穿上车队队服。
自2000年以“F1 in Schools”之名创立以来，STEM Racing一直致力于为有天赋的孩子们提供机会，通过一系列高要求的竞赛激发他们的工程好奇心并磨练技能。
三到六名学生组成的小组需要设计并制造一辆由二氧化碳气瓶驱动的微型F1赛车。目标是以最高70公里/小时的速度，让赛车尽可能快地跑完20米赛道。地区赛和全国赛的获胜者将获得年度世界总决赛的席位，与来自世界各地的顶尖队伍一较高下。
2026年新加坡站是迄今规模最大的一届，共有来自36个不同国家的91支学生队伍参赛，角逐多个不同奖项，以评判他们的实力。
尽管赛车尺寸迷你，但比赛本身与一级方程式赛车（F1）的相似之处远不止一点点。各车队可以自由使用专业计算机辅助设计（CAD）软件自行设计和制造赛车，在降低赛车风阻的过程中检验自己的空气动力学知识。
最终成品在数控铣床（CNC router）上制造，前后翼先进行3D打印，然后组装、喷漆，最后投入比赛。赛车必须遵守严格的规则手册，并且像真正的赛车一样通过车检。
但车队也会因赛道外的技能而受到评判。车队必须制作营销作品集和赞助计划、打造品牌、向评委进行口头陈述，并搭建维修区展位，将所有这些整合成一件令人印象深刻的产品。每支车队最多六名学生，没有任何人可以置身事外。
对于晋级世界总决赛并面临新加坡之行的车队来说，营销和资金问题变得尤为突出——对于一支最多六名成员外加其老师或成人指导的队伍来说，这可不是一笔便宜的开销。
在2026年总决赛举办地圣淘沙名胜世界的大型宴会厅里漫步，很难不被现场展现出的竞技水平、创造力和热情所震撼。
德国Spectrum车队的诺亚表示：“我认为积累经验很重要，但我也热爱竞技本身。你确实能学到如何在压力下作为团队协作。”该车队最终登上领奖台第三名。
另一边，来自新加坡Nebula车队的队长兼设计工程师阿拉夫说，他很享受与来自各国的同龄人见面并向他们学习。而就像一位真正的F1设计师一样，他在查看竞争对手时早已用眼睛“偷师”。他说：“这里的水平非常高。看到其他车队如何解决同样的问题，真的很有意思。”
鉴于大多数参赛者年龄尚小，这条路径并不能直通F1，但该计划得到了F1及其许多车队的支持。许多STEM Racing的校友都利用这项赛事作为跳板，进入相关大学学位，并随后在F1车队中获得一席之地。
希腊的基里亚科斯·塞奥法尼迪斯在2016年赢得了该赛事，目前是红牛福特动力总成公司的一名机械工程师。来自澳大利亚的詹姆斯·米切尔在2003年还参加了世界总决赛，之后被阿斯顿·马丁招致麾下。同为STEM Racing校友的英国人劳伦斯·瓦因斯现在在威廉姆斯担任结构设计工程师，同时仍为该赛事本身工作，担任评论员、导师和评委。
“我想在F1工作，15岁时我给所有车队写信申请工作经验，”瓦因斯告诉Motorsport.com。“由于在这项运动里没有任何人脉，我根本不知道入行的途径是什么，直到我偶然发现了这项赛事。当时还叫F1 in Schools，威廉姆斯与之合作运营其工程学院的培训项目，他们会在你的学业期间提供支持，我知道那就是我的入行之路。”
瓦因斯说这项赛事帮助了他，因为它让他更早地熟悉了计算机辅助设计、计算流体力学和有限元分析模拟等工具和方法。“在参加之前，我不知道那些东西是什么。我直到上大学才会接触到它们，”他说。“15岁时，我在做我的第一个计算机辅助设计，设计这辆微型赛车。在规则之下，这些规则为你从事F1之类的工作打下了非常好的基础。规则超过70页，细节非常多。”
艾米·马丁利用这项赛事攻读工程学位，之后转投金融领域。这些热情最终交汇在一起，她加入了梅赛德斯高性能动力总成公司担任财务总监。
“一开始我对F1其实没那么感兴趣，”她说。“我只是在学校里把朋友们聚到一起，那年世界总决赛上我们是少数几支全女子车队之一。我们赢得营销奖后，我在2016年被选入威廉姆斯工程学院的青训项目。他们带我们进入围场，我在那里见到了尼科·罗斯伯格。就在那时，我下定决心，无论如何都要进入F1。”
“对一个16岁的女孩来说，能身临其境、展望自己未来可能的样子，真的令人无比振奋。”
当被问及她觉得自己从这项赛事中收获了什么时，她回答说：“信心是最主要的。当你让一个15或16岁的孩子在世界级F1工程师和评委面前做展示时，那相当不容易。这会培养出一种无所畏惧的气质。
“而且有些参赛孩子的水平……哇。他们不仅极其聪明，还能在世界舞台上清晰表达自己，说实话这非常棒。这造就了一些非常出色的全面发展型人才。”
不过，STEM Racing 不仅对参与的学生大有裨益，对 F1 车队本身而言，其重要性也在日益提升。在预算帽时代，识别并吸引下一代工程人才的工作开始得越来越早，大多数车队都已建立自己的工程青训学院、毕业生培养计划及其他实习项目，这并非巧合。
“所有车队都意识到年轻人才在团队中的重要性。新想法和新成员能带来巨大贡献，”迈凯伦赛事总监兰迪·辛格告诉 Motorsport.com。“我们在迈凯伦有一套非常成熟的毕业生培养计划，许多从该计划走出来的人这个周末就在赛道上，比如奥斯卡的性能工程师和我们的首席策略师。这是为车队引进顶尖人才的一种非常好的方式。”
“像 STEM Racing 这样的项目对那个年龄段的孩子非常有用，因为它能教你很多关于 F1 车队如何运作的知识。其中有设计、有研究，也有市场和商业方面。这些都是非常有用的经验。”
当被问及对有志于在 F1 或更广泛的赛车运动领域工作的青少年有何建议时，辛格回答说：“只要你参与某种深度的技术性工作，并且是以团队形式合作，无论是 STEM Racing、大学生方程式、火箭项目，甚至是将某项运动练到非常高的水平——这本身也相当有技术含量——那么我认为这确实能让你为在 F1 这样快节奏的团队环境中工作做好充分准备。
“我当然不会限制人们只走某一条路线，但这类事情对人们的申请有很大影响。有时候，处理团队的功能失调是一件关键的事情，而你在大学里直到进入职业环境才真正体验到，所以这非常有用。”
尽管这项赛事与F1的渊源已进入第26个年头，但创始人安德鲁·登福德认为，STEM Racing在2024年品牌重塑后才刚刚开始迎来转机。“你必须教育人们为什么需要在学校教授STEM，”登福德说，他同时也是家族经营的登福德公司的首席执行官，该公司为教育领域供应数控工具。
“我们于2000年启动这个项目，旨在让孩子们对工程和制造产生兴趣，最初是作为‘学校里的捷豹F1’，当他们退出F1时，伯尼·埃克莱斯顿允许我们继续使用F1的名称。这真的占据了我的全部生活。我们现在有77个国家参与该项目。水平不断提高。我得小心不要开始讲技术术语，因为他们会把我彻底比下去。”
F1在Netflix之后的 popularity 热潮也使得该项目的数字上升，STEM Racing现在在其路径中增加了几个入门级学校项目，面向年仅六岁的儿童，复杂程度各不相同。
当被问及他希望孩子们从STEM Racing中获得什么时，登福德说：“我们希望他们能发现自己的技能所在。如果你看看所有的职位角色——车队领队、空气动力学专家、制造工程师、市场营销或项目经理——他们会在那个六人团队中找到自己想做的事。”
“然后他们可以发展所学，并将其带入更广阔的世界。”
2026年决赛选手的未来去向尚不确定。有些人会进入F1围场、航空航天行业，或者走上一条截然不同、毫不相关的职业道路，这条道路甚至还未出现在地平线上。
但无论那条路是什么，他们都将带着在新加坡的经历以及一路磨练的技能，充满能量地迎接未来。
detailEn: Inside the competition building F1’s future engineering talent

As hundreds of students from around the world competed in Singapore at the STEM Racing World Final, the long-running engineering competition is gaining relevance as a potential pathway into Formula 1 and motorsports
Six Saudi Arabian high school students, four boys and two girls, are excitedly pacing around the Singapore F1 paddock.

They are known as Team Lynx Racing, the recently crowned winner of the annual STEM Racing World Finals, which was held in Singapore during the week leading up to the grand prix. Coming out on top of an international, four-day engineering competition, Lynx Racing received the 2026 trophy on the actual grand prix podium as they met the likes of two-time world champion Fernando Alonso and enjoyed an Aston Martin garage tour.
Some of them are hoping that it's not the last time they see an F1 garage up close - the next time, donning a team kit.

Since its inception in 2000 under the F1 in Schools moniker, STEM Racing has aimed to  offer opportunities to talented children to pique their engineering curiosity and hone their skills through a demanding series of competitions.

Groups of three to six students are tasked with designing and manufacturing a miniature F1 car, powered by CO2 cartridges. The goal is to launch the car across a 20-metre track as quickly as possible at speeds of up to 70km/h. Winners of the regional and national competitions claim a place at the annual world finals to take on the best teams from around the world.
The 2026 edition in Singapore was the biggest one yet, with 91 student teams from 36 different countries represented, competing for a number of different awards judging their prowess.

Despite the cars' miniature sizes, the competition itself bears more than just a passing resemblance to F1. Teams are free to design and manufacture the cars themselves using professional CAD software, putting their knowledge of aerodynamics to the test as they shave drag off their cars.

The end product is manufactured on a CNC router, with the front and rear wings being 3D printed before being assembled, painted and finally raced. Adhering to a strict rulebook, cars must all pass scrutineering like a real race car would.

But they are also judged on off-track skills. Teams have to build a marketing portfolio and sponsorship plan, create a brand, hold verbal presentations to judges and build a pit booth display to combine all of that into an impressive product. And with a maximum of six students per team, there is no place to hide.

The question of marketing and funding becomes especially pertinent for teams who make it to the World Final and face a trip to Singapore, which is not an inexpensive undertaking for a group of up to six members plus their teacher or adult guide.
Strolling around the large ballroom of the Resort World Sentosa, where the 2026 finals are held, it's hard not to be taken aback by the level of competition, creativity and passion on display.

"I think it's important to gain experience, but I also love the competition element," says Noah of German team Spectrum, which would go on to take the third podium spot. "You really learn to work under pressure as a team."

Elsewhere, Aarav, team leader and design engineer at team Nebula from Singapore, said he enjoyed meeting and learning from his international peers. And like a true F1 designer, he was already stealing with his eyes as he checked on the competition. "The level here is so high," he said. "It is really interesting to see how other teams solve the same problems."

While there is no direct path to F1 given the age of most competitors, the initiative is supported by F1 and many of its teams. Many STEM Racing alumni have used the competition as a springboard to a relevant university degree and subsequently a place on an F1 team.

Greece's Kyriakos Theofanidis won the event in 2016 and is currently a mechanical engineer at Red Bull Ford Powertrains. James Mitchell from Australia competed at the World Finals as recently as 2003 before being snapped up by Aston Martin. Fellow STEM Racing alumnus Britain's Laurence Vines now works at Williams as a structural design engineer and still works for the event itself as a pundit, mentor and judge.

"I wanted to work in F1 and when I was 15 I wrote letters to all of the teams applying for work experience," Vines told Motorsport.com. "Not having any connections in the sport, I just had no clue what the way in was until I discovered the competition by coincidence. In partnership with what was then called F1 in Schools, Williams ran its engineering academy where they'd support you through your studies, and I knew that was my way in."

Vines says the competition helped him because it familiarised him with tools and methods like CA, CFD and FEA simulations much earlier. "Before I took part I didn't know what those things were. I wouldn't have touched them until university," he said. "At 15, I'm doing my first CAD, designing this miniature car. Under regulations which set you up so well to work in something like Formula 1. They're over 70 pages long with lots of detail.

Amy Martin used the competition to pursue an engineering degree, before switching to the financial world. Those passions eventually collided as she joined Mercedes High Performance Powertrains as a financial controller.

"At the start I wasn't really that interested in F1," she said. "I just got my friends together in school and we were one of the few all-girl teams at the World Finals that year. After we won the Marketing Award, I got selected for the Williams Engineering Academy in 2016. They took us into the paddock where I met Nico Rosberg. That was when I decided I would do anything to get into F1.
"For a 16-year-old girl, it was genuinely electrifying to be there and look at what my future could look like."

When asked what she felt she got out of the competition, she replied: "Confidence is the main thing. When you're asking someone who's 15 or 16 to hold a presentation in front of world-class F1 engineers and judges, that's pretty tough. It instills a level of fearlessness.

"And the standard of some of the kids who compete... wow. They are not just so incredibly intelligent, but to be able to articulate themselves on a world stage, it's honestly great. It has created some really good all-rounders."

STEM Racing isn't just a boon for the students taking part, though, but it's also growing in importance for F1 teams themselves. In a budget cap world, identifying and attracting the next generation of engineering talent has started earlier and earlier, and it's no coincidence the majority of teams have established their own engineering academies, graduate schemes and other placement programmes.

"All teams realise the importance of young talent in the team. New ideas and people contribute so much," McLaren's racing director Randy Singh told Motorsport.com. "We have a very established graduate scheme at McLaren and many of the people who've come off that scheme are here at track this weekend, like Oscar's performance engineer and our lead strategist. It's a really good way of getting super talent into the team.

"Things like STEM Racing are super useful for kids of that age because it teaches you a lot about how a Formula 1 team works. There's design, there's research, there's marketing and commercial aspects as well. That's all really useful experience."

When asked what his advice is to teenagers aspiring to work in F1 or the wider motorsport world, Singh replied: "As long as you're involved in some kind of deep technical endeavor where you work as a team, whether it's STEM Racing, Formula Student, rocketry, or even doing sports to a very high level can be in itself fairly technical, then I think that really equips you well to work in a fast-paced team environment like F1.

"I certainly wouldn't limit people to one route or another, but these kinds of things make a big difference to people's applications. Sometimes, dealing with the dysfunctions of a team is a key thing that you don't really experience at university until you get to a professional environment, so that's super useful."

Despite the event's long affiliation with F1 into its 26th year, founder Andrew Denford feels STEM Racing is only now starting to turn a corner following its 2024 rebrand. "You've got to educate people on why they need to teach STEM in school," said Denford, who is also the CEO of the family-run Denford company which supplies CNC tools to the education sector."

"We started this in 2000 to get kids interested in engineering and manufacturing, first as Jaguar F1 in schools and when they pulled out of F1, Bernie Ecclestone allowed us to keep using the F1 name. It's just consumed my life, really. We've now got 77 countries who are involved in the programme. The level keeps getting higher. I've got to be careful I don't start talking technical terms, because they'll just blow me out of the water."

F1's popularity boom post-Netflix has also seen the programme's numbers go up, with STEM Racing now adding several entry-level school programmes to its pathway for children as young as six, with varying degrees of complexity.

When asked what he wants children to get out of STEM Racing, Denford said: "We want them to find out what their skill set is. If you look at all the job roles; team principal, aerodynamicist, manufacturing engineer, marketing or project manager, they'll find within that team of six what they want to do.
"Then they can develop what they've learned and take it into the wider world."

Wherever the future may take any of the 2026 finalists is up in the air. Some will make it to the F1 paddock, the aerospace industry, or take a wildly different and unrelated career path that hasn't even emerged on the horizon yet.
But whatever that path may be, they will take on the future supercharged by their Singapore experience and the skills they honed along the way.

detailZh: 维斯塔潘与汉密尔顿的父亲安东尼·汉密尔顿在Portimao的GT世界挑战赛欧洲周末期间意外重逢，这一幕赢得了F1粉丝的广泛赞誉。
粉丝们对维斯塔潘与汉密尔顿的父亲安东尼·汉密尔顿在GT世界挑战赛欧洲周末的意外会面反应热烈。
赛车文化超越赛道。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计以及那些让赛车运动不仅仅是运动的故事。
维斯塔潘与汉密尔顿的父亲安东尼·汉密尔顿在Portimao的GT世界挑战赛欧洲周末期间意外重逢，这一幕赢得了F1粉丝的广泛赞誉。
荷兰人在F1赛历中的空档期参加了GT世界挑战赛欧洲总决赛，与克里斯·卢尔汉和本·巴尼科特一起参赛。三人最终在比赛中排名第9。
汉密尔顿先生在庆祝他在赛车运动中度过35周年之际，参加了本周末的GT世界赛事的第一场GT世界赛事。
汉密尔顿先生在Instagram上写道：“很高兴与我的朋友们马克斯和瓦伦蒂诺·罗西见面，谈论赛车运动、生活和家庭。附上与维斯塔潘和瓦伦蒂诺·罗西的合影，他们也在这次赛事中参赛。”
“在赛车运动中度过35年，这是我第一次参加GT世界赛事。多么美好的一天！61辆赛车在起跑线上。多么壮观，多么震撼。向斯蒂芬·拉特和惊人的SRO团队表示衷心的感谢。”
“我很少拍照，但昨天我破例了……三位绝对绅士。”
“粉丝们迅速在社交媒体上对此刻做出反应，将其描述为‘随意’和‘纯真’。”,
纯真。难道安东尼不是一般的大赛车迷吗？老一辈的赛车迷似乎很尊重马克斯。他可能很容易相处，并且有相似的喜好。记得杰克·伊克斯说过，马克斯认出他并过来聊天，这在年轻车手中间并不常见，
一位粉丝在Reddit上评论道。
“这个人真是太好了。为了给刘易斯实现他梦寐以求的生活，他做了所有的事情，尽管他们当时没什么钱。所有你听说的小事。在2021年立即祝贺马克斯。在哈吉亚出事故后安慰他。现在又是这样。他看起来就像一个真正的好人，”另一位粉丝评论道，而另一个人写道：“他也在维斯塔潘的维修区里。太随机了，也太酷了。”
detailEn: Max Verstappen and Anthony Hamilton's "wholesome" reunion earns F1 fan praise
Fans react to Max Verstappen's surprise paddock meeting with Lewis Hamilton's father, Anthony Hamilton, at the GT World Challenge Europe weekend
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton's father, Anthony Hamilton, shared a surprise paddock meeting during the GT World Challenge Europe weekend in Portimao, which has drawn widespread praise from Formula 1 fans.
The Dutchman used a gap in the F1 calendar to compete in the GT World Challenge Europe finale alongside Chris Lulham and Ben Barnicoat. The trio finished ninth in the race.
Hamilton Sr., who was celebrating 35 years in motorsport, attended his first GT World event during the race weekend.

"Great to catch up with my friends Max and Valentino Rossi, talking all things motorsport, life and family," Hamilton Sr. wrote on Instagram alongside photos of him with Verstappen and Valentino Rossi, who was also racing in the event.
"35 years in motorsport and my first ever GT World event. What a day! 61 cars on the grid. What a sight, what a sound. Huge thanks to Stéphane Ratel and the amazing SRO team.
"I rarely take photos, but yesterday I made an exception… three absolute gentlemen."
Fans were quick to react to the moment on social media, describing it as both "random" and "wholesome".

"Wholesome. Isn't Anthony a big motorsport fan in general? Older motorsport people seem to respect Max quite a bit. He's probably pretty easy to talk to and has similar preferences. Remember Jacky Ickx saying that Max recognises him and comes to chat, which isn't common amongst young drivers," one fan commented on Reddit.

Someone else posted: "I don't know much about Lewis's dad, other than he's a stand-up guy. There were a few times when he was a spare dad to one of the new rookies who just needed a kind human being, and Anthony was it. Btw, it seems that Max is cut from the same fabric."

"Man, the guy is so wholesome. Everything he did to get Lewis the life he dreamed of, even though they had little money. All the small things you hear. Congratulating Max in 2021 right away. Consoling Hadjar after his crash. Now this. He seems like just a genuinely good person," another fan commented, while someone else wrote: "He was in Verstappen’s garage as well. So random and cool."

items.originalTitle: Horner was congratulated by Red Bull bosses after F1 engine's wins
items.summaryEn: Christian Horner said he received congratulations from Red Bull's majority shareholders and company CEO Oliver Mintzlaff after the Formula 1 team's first wins with its in-house engine. The Red Bull Powertrains division, initially set up to take over Honda engines, ultimately became a manufacturer in its own right for the 2026 rules cycle.
detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳表示，红牛自研引擎为F1车队取得首胜后，他收到了红牛多数股东和公司CEO奥利弗·明茨拉夫的祝贺。
红牛动力总成部门是为应对本田2021年底退出F1的决定而设立，最初负责接手那些本田引擎，最终在2026规则周期成为独立制造商。
其首款动力单元从一开始就具备竞争力——以至于在新版2026额外研发与升级机会机制下，红牛被判为拥有围场最佳动力单元，这一判定存在一定争议；该机制只计算内燃机的性能。
该动力单元在第16场大奖赛成为分站冠军得主：马克斯·维斯塔潘在马来西亚举行的巴林大奖赛夺冠，一周后又在加坡赢得冲刺赛和正赛，复制了这一结果。
霍纳曾是红牛车队的创始车队领队，直到去年夏天被解职，他在红牛动力总成项目获得批准的过程中发挥了重要作用，并告诉The Race的Edd Straw和Jon Noble，他的贡献已得到Mintzlaff等人的认可，而他在任期间与Mintzlaff关系并不融洽。
在The Race F1播客中被问及如果他仍是车队领队，是否会对他今年观察到的情况做出不同处理时，霍纳表示：“这没法说，不是吗？”
“我认为这支车队是我组建和打造的车队，股东们，甚至在新加坡和马来西亚的最后一场胜利之后，他们两人都分别感谢了我，并提到了这一事实。而Oliver Mintzlaff在新加坡站比赛后非常客气地打电话给我，感谢我所组建的团队以及他们后来取得的成就。
“所以我认为随着时间推移，你也会获得更全面的视角。红牛现在显然处于不同的境地，就其运作方式而言，这是自然的，当像主席这样的人物——那是Dietrich Mateschitz，那就是红牛——不再存在时。
“但据我所知，这项业务正在飞速发展；他们的增长表现令人难以置信。所以我能做的真的就是祝他们未来一切顺利。”
霍纳在红牛动力总成成立时表示，已故的红牛联合创始人迪特里希·马特希茨已经表明他“不怕冒险”，并补充说，尽管红牛在底盘方面“从未想过我们能够取得多年来所实现的成就”，“现在的挑战是尝试在动力单元领域复制这一点”。
他告诉The Race，成立红牛动力总成是一个“荒谬的想法”，该公司与福特合作开展2026年发动机项目，并补充说马特希茨和红牛联合所有者Chalerm Yoovidhya值得称赞，因为红牛内部有人问“我们到底为什么要做这件事？”
“但这向我证明了一点，再次通过运用那种理念——把一群优秀的人聚集在一起，赋予他们权力，给他们明确的方向，创造正确的文化，给他们工具……我们在55周内把一家气泡膜工厂改造成了一座发动机工厂，”霍纳说道，他正在其回忆录《Drive》发布前对媒体发言。
“那台引擎在它的首个赛季就被评为一级方程式赛车中最具性能的引擎，并在第16次尝试时获胜，可以说，我认为这是我效力红牛期间最大的成就之一。
“而且，这再次向我展示了人、文化以及每个人都专注于同一目标的力量。”
霍纳曾同时担任红牛车队的领队和首席执行官，但在马特希茨于2022年10月去世后，一场内部权力斗争实际上在霍纳与明茨拉夫（正式职务为企业项目首席执行官）以及红牛前赛车运动顾问赫尔穆特·马尔科之间展开。
在2024年经历了一场个人丑闻后——当时红牛在对一名员工不当行为的独立调查证明霍纳无过错后选择继续留任他——霍纳在2025年7月英国大奖赛后遭解除职务。
当被问及在人们认为红牛正变成“霍纳的车队”的背景下，他是否在塑造车队的方式上用力过猛时，他说：“是的，这就是我被告知的。这是赫尔穆特最后告诉我的。”
“回头看，总有一些你会做得不同的事情，或者……就像你审视的每一场比赛，你会有不同的表现。有没有我本可以做得不同的事情？有。我是否忠于我的信念、忠于我自己？我认为我是的。”
“我被要求放弃部分职责，我觉得那会损害车队领导层的角色。所以我说我不准备那样做。”
“也许这促成了最终的决定。但对我来说，那不会是正确的做法。但这就是生活，不是吗？”
“我和两位股东（Yoovidhya 和 Mark Mateschitz）的关系还不错，我很感激他们的评论和留言。我离开后见过他们两位。现在这多少已经是过去的事了。和 Oliver 也一样，我现在能做的就是祝他们未来一切顺利。”
“这是我人生中的一个篇章，我为自己所做的事感到自豪，为自己取得的成就感到自豪，回首在那里的时光，90% 都让我充满美好的回忆。”
克里斯蒂安·霍纳的《DRIVE》一书将于 10 月 22 日由 Bantam 出版：https://www.amazon.co.uk/gp/product/1911754785
克里斯蒂安将在英国各地巡回分享书中的故事（诺丁汉 10 月 19 日周一、巴斯 10 月 20 日、伦敦 10 月 26 日）。订票请访问：https://www.ticketmaster.co.uk/christian-horner-tickets/artist/5672765
detailEn: Christian Horner says he was congratulated by Red Bull majority shareholders and the company's CEO Oliver Mintzlaff in the wake of its Formula 1 team's first wins with its in-house engine.

The Red Bull Powertrains division that was established in response to Honda's decision to withdraw from F1 at the end of 2021, at first to take over those Honda engines, ultimately ended up becoming a manufacturer in its own right for the 2026 rules cycle.

Its first power unit has been competitive from the off - to the extent that Red Bull has been judged somewhat controversially to have the best in the field under the new-for-2026 Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities mechanism, a system that only accounts for the performance of the internal combustion engine.
It became a race winner in its 16th grand prix as Max Verstappen won the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, a result he repeated by then winning the sprint race and main event in Singapore a week later.

Horner, Red Bull's founding team principal until his dismissal in summer last year, played an important role in the Red Bull Powertrains project receiving the green light and told The Race's Edd Straw and Jon Noble his contribution had been recognised by the likes of Mintzlaff, with whom he had a difficult relationship while in post.
Asked on The Race F1 Podcast whether he would have done anything differently to what he had observed this year were he still team principal, Horner said: "That's impossible to say, isn't it?

"I think the team is the team that I've put together and built and the shareholders, even after the last victory in Singapore and Malaysia, both of them have independently thanked me and made reference to that fact. And Oliver Mintzlaff very graciously called me after the race in Singapore to thank me for what I've put together and what they've gone on to achieve.

"So I think with time you get perspective as well. Red Bull's just in a different place now, obviously, in terms of how it's operating, which is natural when a presence like the chairman, that was Dietrich Mateschitz, that was Red Bull, is no longer there.
"But the business is, from what I understand, flying; they're doing incredibly, growth-wise. So all I can do is really wish them the best of luck for the future."

Horner said at the time of Red Bull Powertrains' establishment that the late Red Bull co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz had shown he was "not afraid of risk" and added that while Red Bull "never thought we could have done what we've managed to achieve over the years" with its chassis, "the challenge now is to try and replicate that within the power unit".

He told The Race that it was a "harebrained idea" to set up Red Bull Powertrains, which partnered with Ford for the 2026 engine project, adding that Mateschitz and Red Bull co-owner Chalerm Yoovidhya deserved credit because there were people within Red Bull asking "Why the hell are we doing this?".

"But it demonstrated to me that, again, by applying that philosophy of getting a great group of people together, empowering them, giving them clear direction and creating the right culture, giving them the tools...we converted a bubble wrap factory into an engine facility in 55 weeks," said Horner, who is speaking to media ahead of the launch of his memoir, Drive.

"For that engine to go out and be judged to be the most performant engine in Formula 1 in its debut year and win on its 16th attempt, arguably, I see that as one of my biggest achievements during my time at Red Bull.
"And again, it demonstrates to me the power of people, culture, and just everybody being focused on the same objective."

Horner held the dual role of team principal and CEO of Red Bull Racing but following the death of Mateschitz in October 2022 an internal power struggle emerged effectively between Horner and Mintzlaff - officially the CEO of corporate projects - plus Helmut Marko, Red Bull's former motorsport advisor.

Having survived a personal scandal in 2024, when Red Bull chose to stick with him after an independent investigation of misconduct against a member of staff cleared him of wrongdoing, Horner was relieved of his duties after the British Grand Prix in July 2025.

Asked whether he had overplayed his hand in the way he had shaped the team, in the context of perceptions that Red Bull was becoming 'Team Horner', he said: "Yeah, and that's what I was told. That's what Helmut told me, at the end.

"You look back, there's always things that you would have done differently or...it's like every race you looked at, you would have performed differently. Is there things that I could have done differently? Yes. Was I true to my beliefs and true to myself? I think I was.
"I was asked to give up parts of the role and I felt it would compromise the role of the leadership of the team. And so I said I wasn't prepared to do that.
"And maybe that contributed to the final decision. But for me, it wouldn't have been the right thing to do. But that's life, isn't it?

"I have a decent relationship with both shareholders [Yoovidhya and Mark Mateschitz], I was grateful for their comments and their messages. I've seen both of them since I left. It's kind of water under the bridge now. And with Oliver as well, it's all I can do is wish them the best for the future now.
"It's a chapter of my life that I'm proud of what I did and proud of what I achieved and will look back with great fondness of 90% of my time there."
DRIVE by Christian Horner will be published on 22nd October by Bantam: https://www.amazon.co.uk/gp/product/1911754785

Christian will be sharing stories from the book on tour across the UK (Nottingham Mon 19th, Bath 20th, London 26th October). To book tickets visit: https://www.ticketmaster.co.uk/christian-horner-tickets/artist/5672765

detailZh: Stray Kids成员Felix晒法拉利F1幕后照片，令粉丝沸腾
Stray Kids成员Felix分享了新加坡大奖赛到访法拉利车队的新幕后照片
致法拉利车迷。来自马拉内罗及更广范围的最新法拉利F1新闻、车手动态、技术分析与比赛反应。
Stray Kids成员Felix分享了新加坡大奖赛期间到访法拉利的幕后照片，法拉利车队也发布了这位K-pop明星在维修区的视频。
韩国组合Stray Kids成员Felix上周末作为法拉利一级方程式车队的嘉宾，现身滨海湾赛道。在随法拉利车队度过一段时间后，他在Instagram上发布了多张此次活动的幕后照片。
“法拉利幕后，”Felix写道。截至10月18日，该帖子已获得超过64.8万个赞和6000条评论。
此前他还发布了比赛日帖子，只写了：“Forza 法拉利。”该帖子获得了超过200万个赞。
法拉利亚太区账号在比赛周末前已通过联合帖子预告了他的到访。“从赛道到舞台。因赛车而团结，因激情而驱动，”帖子写道。
车队也发布了他们自己拍摄的这次到访视频。法拉利的短片配文写道：“跟随@yong.lixx 参观车库。”
一位粉丝写道：“Felix 随意地把我们介绍给法拉利，就好像我们现在都是围场的一员了。我爱死了！！”
另一位说：“Felix 真的很高兴能到那里。Forza 法拉利！”第三位则补充道：“我能感受到他对他们的真心支持。”
有些粉丝见到车手也同样激动。一位粉丝发帖写道：“FELIUIXXXX 啊啊啊啊啊，还有我的神夏尔，我要尖叫了。”
费利克斯的造型也引起了关注。我们在赛后整理的手表盘点中，注意到了他佩戴的愛彼皇家橡树计时码表50周年纪念款，41毫米玫瑰金材质，估值在11.2万至11.8万美元之间。
这次到访正值这位歌手忙碌的一个月。10月初，他曾在路易威登2027春夏大秀现场发帖，还为美妆品牌赫拉出镜了一支“跟我一起准备”视频。
法拉利在滨海湾赛道的比赛喜忧参半。夏尔·勒克莱尔落后于马克斯·维斯塔潘获得第二，而刘易斯·汉密尔顿因策略冒险失败仅列第六。
车队在前往奥斯汀参加美国大奖赛时位列车队积分榜第二，该赛事将于10月23日至25日举行。
detailEn: Stray Kids' Felix sends fans into frenzy with behind-the-scenes Ferrari F1 photos
Stray Kids star Felix has shared new behind-the-scenes photos from his Singapore Grand Prix visit
For Ferrari fans. The latest Scuderia Ferrari F1 news, driver updates, technical analysis and race reaction from Maranello and beyond.
Stray Kids' Felix has shared behind-the-scenes photos from his time with Ferrari at the Singapore Grand Prix, and the team has posted its own footage of the K-pop star in the garage.

Felix, a member of the South Korean group Stray Kids, was a guest of the Ferrari Formula 1 team at Marina Bay circuit last weekend. Following his time with the Scuderia, he posted to Instagram a number of behind-the-scenes photos of the occasion.
"Ferrari behind the scenes," Felix wrote. By 18 October the post had more than 648,000 likes and 6,000 comments.
It followed his race day post, which simply read: "Forza Ferrari." That had more than two million likes.
Ferrari's Asia-Pacific account had already teased his visit with a joint post before the race weekend. "From the circuit to the stage. United by racing, driven by passion," it read.
The team also published its own video of the visit. "Following @yong.lixx around the garage," the Ferrari reel was captioned.
Felix's fans, known as Stays, quickly filled the comments.
"Felix casually introducing us to Ferrari like we're all part of the paddock now. I love it!!" one fan wrote.
"Felix is so genuinely happy to be there. Forza Ferrari!" said another, while a third added: "I can feel his genuine support for them."
Some were just as excited to see the drivers. "FELIUIXXXX AAHHHHH AND MY GOAT CHARLES IM SCREAMING," one fan posted.

Felix's look drew attention too. Our round-up of the watches worn at the race brought attention to his Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Chronograph 50th Anniversary in 41mm rose gold, valued at between $112,000 and $118,000.
The visit came in a busy month for the singer. Earlier in October, he posted from Louis Vuitton's Spring/Summer 2027 show, and he also appeared in a "get ready with me" video for beauty brand Hera.
Ferrari had a mixed race at Marina Bay. Charles Leclerc finished second behind Max Verstappen, while Lewis Hamilton was sixth after a strategy gamble backfired.
The team is second in the constructors' championship heading to the United States Grand Prix in Austin, which runs from 23 to 25 October.

他此行是作为法拉利F1车队的嘉宾，到访滨海湾赛道

He was a guest of the Ferrari Formula 1 team at the Marina Bay circuit.

items.originalTitle: Documentary on Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso's F1 rivalry reportedly in the works
items.summaryEn: Former Spanish F1 commentator Antonio Lobato claims the BBC is working on a documentary about the fierce 2007 McLaren rivalry between Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso; the BBC has not yet confirmed the project.
detailZh: 关于刘易斯·汉密尔顿与费尔南多·阿隆索F1竞争的纪录片据称正在制作中
一名前西班牙F1评论员声称，BBC正在制作一部关于刘易斯·汉密尔顿与费尔南多·阿隆索2007年在迈凯伦那段臭名昭著的内斗的纪录片
刘易斯·汉密尔顿，迈凯伦，费尔南多·阿隆索，迈凯伦
赛道之外的赛车文化。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计，以及让赛车不止于运动的故事。
据前西班牙F1评论员安东尼奥·洛瓦托透露，BBC正在制作一部关于刘易斯·汉密尔顿和费尔南多·阿隆索2007年在迈凯伦共度的混乱赛季的纪录片。
洛瓦托目前是西班牙网站SoyMotor.com的联合总监，本周早些时候他在该媒体的Twitch频道上讨论了这一据称的项目。需要指出的是，BBC尚未确认这部纪录片。
“这件事肯定会被讲述出来。问题是……会讲述什么？因为我知道BBC正在准备一部纪录片，”他说。
洛瓦托曾是西班牙F1转播的解说员，见证了阿隆索最辉煌的赛季——2005年和2006年他随雷诺争夺两届世界冠军，以及2007年他在迈凯伦的那一年。
“他们邀请我参与，我拒绝了邀请，”他谈到这部纪录片时说。“我不想卷入那些故事。我知道我经历过什么，我知道发生了什么，也许从我的角度来看，这也可能有些失真，当纪录片出来时，我想看看。”
他补充说，其他报道那个赛季的记者也将参与。
“我知道还有其他记者同事，那一年他们也在场，他们会参与，会在那里讲述部分发生的事情。我们看看他们如何对待它，如何制作，以及那个故事如何被讲述。”
刘易斯·汉密尔顿，迈凯伦，费尔南多·阿隆索，迈凯伦
2007赛季仍然是锦标赛历史上最具戏剧性的赛季之一。阿隆索以两届卫冕冠军的身份来到迈凯伦，而汉密尔顿在他身旁完成首秀，希望一上来就能迅速进入状态。
随着赛季的推进，紧张气氛不断加剧，最终彻底爆发：两人在赛季结束时同积109分，落后于夺得冠军的基米·莱科宁一分。迈凯伦还因“间谍门”事件被排除在车队锦标赛之外，而阿隆索在赛季结束后离开，重返雷诺。
将近20年后，两位车手仍在参赛。汉密尔顿代表法拉利，以229分在2026年车手积分榜上排名第三。阿隆索如今效力于阿斯顿·马丁，处境艰难，仅积7分。
两人都将出现在10月23日至25日于奥斯汀举行的美国大奖赛发车格上。
detailEn: Documentary on Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso's F1 rivalry reportedly in the works
A former Spanish F1 commentator claims the BBC is working on a documentary about Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso's infamous 2007 McLaren rivalry
Lewis Hamilton, McLaren, Fernando Alonso, McLaren
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
According to former Spanish F1 commentator Antonio Lobato, the BBC is making a documentary about Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso's chaotic 2007 season together at McLaren.

Lobato, who is now the co-director of Spanish website SoyMotor.com, discussed the supposed project on the outlet's Twitch channel earlier this week. It should be noted that the BBC is yet to confirm the documentary.
"It will definitely be told. The question is... what will be told? Because I know the BBC is preparing a documentary," he said.
Lobato was the voice of F1 coverage in Spain during Alonso's greatest seasons as he fought for two championship wins with Renault in 2005 and 2006 and during his year with McLaren in 2007.

"They invited me to take part and I turned the invitation down," he said of the documentary. "I don't want to get involved in those stories. I know what I lived through, I know what happened, perhaps from my point of view, which may also be a bit distorted, and when the documentary comes out, I'd like to watch it."
He added that other journalists who covered that season will be taking part.

"I know there are other journalist colleagues who were there that year who are going to do it, who are going to be there and will tell part of what happened. We'll see how they treat it, how it is made, and how that story is told."
Lewis Hamilton, McLaren, Fernando Alonso, McLaren

The 2007 season remains one of the most dramatic in the history of the championship. Alonso arrived at McLaren as the two-time reigning champion, and Hamilton made his debut alongside him hoping to hit the ground running.

Tension grew as the season continued, and eventually it boiled over as the pair ended on a level 109 points at the end of the season, one point behind Kimi Raikkonen, who won the championship. McLaren was also excluded from the constructors' championship over Spygate, and Alonso left at the end of the season to return to Renault.
Almost 20 years later, both drivers are still racing. Hamilton is third in the 2026 drivers' standings with Ferrari on 229 points. Alonso, now at Aston Martin and struggling, has seven points.
Both will be on the grid at the United States Grand Prix in Austin, which takes place from 23 to 25 October.

keyPointsEn: Lobato is now co-director of the Spanish website SoyMotor.com and discussed the project earlier this week on the outlet's Twitch channel
